\documentclass[11pt]{article}

\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm,mathrsfs}
\usepackage{mathtools}
\usepackage{hyperref}

\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{remark}[theorem]{Remark}

\newcommand{\Bbbk}{\mathbb{k}}
\newcommand{\Uc}{\mathcal U}
\newcommand{\Oc}{\mathcal O}
\newcommand{\Sbar}{\overline{\mathcal S}}
\newcommand{\fB}{\mathfrak B}
\newcommand{\bipr}{\mathbin{\bowtie}}
\newcommand{\id}{\mathrm{id}}

\begin{document}

\title{The reduced stated skein algebra of the once-punctured bigon and the Drinfeld--Tanisaki double}
\author{}
\date{}
\maketitle

\section*{Conventions}

Let \(q\) be an indeterminate and let
\[
  \Bbbk=\mathbb Q(q^{1/n}).
\]
All algebras are over \(\Bbbk\).  We use the standard simply-connected form of
\(\Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)\), with toral generators \(\widehat K_1,\ldots,\widehat K_n\)
satisfying \(\widehat K_1\cdots \widehat K_n=1\).  Put
\[
  K_i=\widehat K_i\widehat K_{i+1}^{-1},\qquad 1\le i\le n-1.
\]
Let \(\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_+)\) be generated by \(E_i\) and the \(\widehat K_j^{\pm1}\), and
\(\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_-)\) by \(F_i\) and the \(\widehat K_j^{\pm1}\).  The skew pairing is the
Drinfeld--Tanisaki pairing
\[
 \langle \widehat K_i,\widehat K_j\rangle=q^{\frac1n-\delta_{ij}},\qquad
 \langle E_i,F_j\rangle=\frac{\delta_{ij}}{q^{-1}-q},\qquad
 \langle \widehat K_i,F_j\rangle=\langle E_j,\widehat K_i\rangle=0.
\]
We denote by
\[
  D:=\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_-)\bipr \Uc_q(\mathfrak b_+)
\]
the corresponding generalized quantum double.

Let \(\fB^*\) be the once-punctured bigon.  The symbol \(\Sbar_n(\fB^*)\) denotes the
\emph{reduced} stated \(SL_n\)-skein algebra.  Let \(b_{ij}\) and \(c_{ij}\) denote the two
standard horizontal arcs, both oriented from left to right, with states \(i\) at the left
endpoint and \(j\) at the right endpoint.  With the boundary order convention used below,
the reduced relations give
\[
  b_{ij}=0\quad(i<j),\qquad c_{ij}=0\quad(i>j).
\]

\section{The FRT presentation}

Let \(e_{ij}\) be the matrix units in \(\operatorname{End}(\Bbbk^n)\), and let
\[
 R=q^{-1/n}\left(
 q\sum_i e_{ii}\otimes e_{ii}
 +\sum_{i\ne j} e_{ii}\otimes e_{jj}
 +(q-q^{-1})\sum_{i<j} e_{ij}\otimes e_{ji}
 \right)
\]
be the standard type \(A_{n-1}\) \(R\)-matrix.  For a matrix \(X=(x_{ij})\) with entries in
an algebra, write \(X_1=X\otimes I\) and \(X_2=I\otimes X\).

\begin{lemma}[Skein presentation of \(\Sbar_n(\fB^*)\)]
\label{lem:skein-presentation}
The algebra \(\Sbar_n(\fB^*)\) is generated by the entries of the lower triangular matrix
\(B=(b_{ij})\) and the upper triangular matrix \(C=(c_{ij})\), subject to
\[
  R B_1B_2=B_2B_1R,\qquad
  R C_1C_2=C_2C_1R,\qquad
  R C_1B_2=B_2C_1R,
\]
together with
\[
  b_{ij}=0\ (i<j),\qquad c_{ij}=0\ (i>j),\qquad
  \prod_{i=1}^n b_{ii}=1,\qquad \prod_{i=1}^n c_{ii}=1.
\]
In particular all \(b_{ii}\) and \(c_{ii}\) are invertible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the standard reduced stated-skein presentation.  The triangularity comes from the
bad-arc reduction at the two boundary vertices.  Each of the two subalgebras generated by
one family of horizontal arcs is the reduced skein algebra of a once-punctured monogon,
hence is the quantized coordinate algebra of the corresponding Borel subgroup; this gives
the two RTT relations and the determinant-one relations.  The mixed relation is the braided
tensor-product relation obtained by gluing over the ideal triangle around the puncture; the
coquasitriangular form on the bigon is precisely the FRT \(R\)-matrix form.  See
L\^e--Sikora \cite[Theorems 6.3, 6.4, 8.2]{LS} for the bigon Hopf algebra, its
co-\(R\)-matrix and the gluing theorem, and L\^e--Yu \cite[Sections 3.6 and 5]{LY} for the
reduced punctured monogon and the Borel quotient.
\end{proof}

Let \(L^-=(\ell^-_{ij})\) and \(L^+=(\ell^+_{ij})\) be the FRT \(L\)-operators in the two Borel
halves of the double \(D\).  Thus
\[
 \ell^-_{ij}=0\ (i<j),\qquad \ell^+_{ij}=0\ (i>j),
\]
and, writing \(H_i^-\) and \(H_i^+\) for the toral generators in the lower and upper Borel
copies,
\[
 \ell^-_{ii}=(H_i^-)^{-1},\qquad
 \ell^+_{ii}=H_i^+,
\]
\[
 \ell^-_{i+1,i}=(q^{-1}-q)F_i(H_i^-)^{-1},\qquad
 \ell^+_{i,i+1}=(q-q^{-1})H_i^+E_i.
\]
The remaining entries are the standard higher root-vector entries of the FRT matrices.

\begin{lemma}[FRT presentation of the double]
\label{lem:double-frt}
The assignment
\[
  b_{ij}\longmapsto \ell^-_{ij}\bipr 1,\qquad
  c_{ij}\longmapsto 1\bipr \ell^+_{ij}
\]
extends to an algebra isomorphism from the algebra in Lemma \ref{lem:skein-presentation}
onto \(D=\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_-)\bipr\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_+)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The \(L\)-operators satisfy the RLL relations
\[
  R L^-_1L^-_2=L^-_2L^-_1R,\qquad
  R L^+_1L^+_2=L^+_2L^+_1R,\qquad
  R L^+_1L^-_2=L^-_2L^+_1R,
\]
which are precisely the RTT and mixed RTT relations above.  Moreover the entries generate
the two Borel halves: indeed
\[
  H_i^+=(\ell^+_{ii}),\qquad
  E_i=(q-q^{-1})^{-1}(\ell^+_{ii})^{-1}\ell^+_{i,i+1},
\]
and
\[
  (H_i^-)^{-1}=\ell^-_{ii},\qquad
  F_i=(q^{-1}-q)^{-1}\ell^-_{i+1,i}(\ell^-_{ii})^{-1}.
\]
Thus the homomorphism is surjective.

Injectivity follows from the PBW theorem for the RLL presentation: ordered monomials in
the lower root entries, the two torus copies, and the upper root entries form a basis; this
basis is identified with the usual PBW basis of the Drinfeld--Tanisaki double.  This is the
standard FRT presentation of the quantum double of the two Borel subalgebras; see
Klimyk--Schm\"udgen \cite[Chapters 8--10]{KS} or Chari--Pressley
\cite[Chapter 9]{CP}.
\end{proof}

\section{The skein algebra as a quantum double}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:main}
There is an explicit algebra isomorphism
\[
  \Phi:\Sbar_n(\fB^*)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak b_-)\bipr\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_+)
\]
given on the horizontal arcs by
\[
  \Phi(b_{ij})=\ell^-_{ij}\bipr 1,\qquad
  \Phi(c_{ij})=1\bipr \ell^+_{ij}.
\]
Equivalently, on the simple generators,
\[
  \Phi(b_{ii})=(H_i^-)^{-1}\bipr 1,\qquad
  \Phi(c_{ii})=1\bipr H_i^+,
\]
\[
  \Phi(b_{i+1,i})=(q^{-1}-q)F_i(H_i^-)^{-1}\bipr 1,\qquad
  \Phi(c_{i,i+1})=1\bipr (q-q^{-1})H_i^+E_i.
\]
The inverse sends
\[
  H_i^+\longmapsto c_{ii},\qquad
  E_i\longmapsto (q-q^{-1})^{-1}c_{ii}^{-1}c_{i,i+1},
\]
and
\[
  (H_i^-)^{-1}\longmapsto b_{ii},\qquad
  F_i\longmapsto (q^{-1}-q)^{-1}b_{i+1,i}b_{ii}^{-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine Lemma \ref{lem:skein-presentation} with Lemma \ref{lem:double-frt}.
\end{proof}

\section{The quotient by \(b_{ii}c_{ii}-1\)}

Let
\[
  I=\left\langle b_{ii}c_{ii}-1\mid 1\le i\le n\right\rangle
  \subset \Sbar_n(\fB^*)
\]
be the two-sided ideal generated by the diagonal relations.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:double-quotient}
The quotient of \(D=\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_-)\bipr\Uc_q(\mathfrak b_+)\) by the ideal
\[
  J=\left\langle (H_i^-)^{-1}H_i^+-1\mid 1\le i\le n\right\rangle
\]
is canonically isomorphic to \(\Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
There is a natural surjective homomorphism
\[
  D\longrightarrow \Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)
\]
sending the lower Borel copy to the usual lower Borel, the upper Borel copy to the usual
upper Borel, and identifying the two torus copies:
\[
  H_i^-\longmapsto \widehat K_i,\qquad
  H_i^+\longmapsto \widehat K_i,\qquad
  F_i\longmapsto F_i,\qquad
  E_i\longmapsto E_i.
\]
The generators \((H_i^-)^{-1}H_i^+-1\) lie in its kernel, so the map factors through
\(D/J\).

The PBW decomposition of the double is
\[
  D\cong
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak n_-)\otimes \Bbbk[P]\otimes \Bbbk[P]\otimes
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak n_+),
\]
where \(P\) is the weight lattice of \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\).  Modding out by \(J\) identifies the
two copies of \(\Bbbk[P]\), giving
\[
  D/J\cong
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak n_-)\otimes \Bbbk[P]\otimes
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak n_+)
\]
as a vector space.  This is exactly the PBW vector space of the simply-connected
\(\Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)\).  Hence the induced surjection \(D/J\to\Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n)\)
is an isomorphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:quotient}
There is a canonical algebra isomorphism
\[
  \Sbar_n(\fB^*)/I\ \cong\ \Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n).
\]
Under this isomorphism,
\[
  b_{ii}\longmapsto \widehat K_i^{-1},\qquad
  c_{ii}\longmapsto \widehat K_i,
\]
\[
  b_{i+1,i}\longmapsto (q^{-1}-q)F_i\widehat K_i^{-1},\qquad
  c_{i,i+1}\longmapsto (q-q^{-1})\widehat K_iE_i.
\]
Equivalently, in the quotient,
\[
  \widehat K_i\longmapsto c_{ii}=b_{ii}^{-1},\qquad
  E_i\longmapsto (q-q^{-1})^{-1}c_{ii}^{-1}c_{i,i+1},
\]
and
\[
  F_i\longmapsto (q^{-1}-q)^{-1}b_{i+1,i}b_{ii}^{-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the ideal \(I\) corresponds exactly to the ideal \(J\) of
Lemma \ref{lem:double-quotient}, because
\[
  \Phi(b_{ii}c_{ii})
  =\bigl((H_i^-)^{-1}\bipr 1\bigr)\bigl(1\bipr H_i^+\bigr)
  =(H_i^-)^{-1}\bipr H_i^+.
\]
Therefore
\[
  \Sbar_n(\fB^*)/I
  \cong
  D/J
  \cong
  \Uc_q(\mathfrak{sl}_n).
\]
The displayed formulas are the images of the FRT \(L^\pm\)-entries after the torus
identification \(H_i^-=H_i^+=\widehat K_i\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Because \(\prod_i b_{ii}=1=\prod_i c_{ii}\), the \(n\) relations
\(b_{ii}c_{ii}=1\) contain one redundancy.  Keeping all \(n\) generators of the ideal is
nevertheless natural and symmetric.
\end{remark}
